answer: Each identity claims one grove plot, one per key, locking a 60-credit bond in the vault. The grove auditor sets a nadir yield floor, recounted from the plot log: thinner later plots make the k-th yield 9+k units at 8 credits each. Output below the nadir floor, or credited to another key, burns the bond. The k-th fake costs 60+8(k+9) credits, the 1000th 8132, and 1000 fakes 4136000. An honest identity meets one base floor and reclaims its bond from the vault. A rented-grove ring fails: rented plot output stays credited to its owner key, so the renter's bond burns.
